He said: "Madueke, no problem, you pulled out, you got injured against Uruguay, it was quite a hard tackle.

"I look at players like Timber, Eze, Odegaard, all pulled out because they didn't play against Manchester City. Those four players, no problem with it.

"But Hincapie, Saka, Rice, Gabriel, Saliba, Trossard, Zubimendi had no problems against Manchester City. I just don't think it's right.

"If I were part of the Premier League and I was making a decision, I would bring in a new rule, you miss the next Premier League game available if you pull out of international duty. I tell you something, players will stop pulling out."

"I get it, Arteta is doing everything possible to win these trophies," Agbonlahor added. "Their next game after the international break is the FA Cup against Southampton.

"I'm just not keen on players pulling out of international duty. It's an honour to play for your country. It doesn't sit right with me."

Sports.title: Football chairman helped stop Wrexham stadium plans then made Racecourse Ground history
Sports.content:
All recommendations within this article are informed by expert editorial opinion. If you click on a link in this story we will earn affiliate revenue.

Wrexham fans dreaming of European football one day returning to the Racecourse can already find a documentary about the last time it happened - by the man who helped keep their ground.

The New Saints owner, Mike Harris, has now even matched the Dragons with a fly-on-the-wall documentary of the Welsh champions.

11 The New Saints have won a record 18th Cymru Premier League title under Harris Credit: Getty

Wrexham's Disney + show has been able to showcase the club's meteoric rise after three straight promotions.

Wrexham stadium plans

Rob McElhenney and Ryan Reynolds are next hoping to oversee a major redevelopment of the Racecourse Ground after receiving an £18million grant in public money to assist with upgrades.

However, any improvements may have been impossible had Wrexham's former owners sold the land on which the site stands.

TNS chairman Harris told talkSPORT that he played a part in the subsequent court ruling that saw the Racecourse remain in the hands of the club's administrators.

"We're only down the road from Wrexham, and so we've had a long sort of knowledge of each other's clubs," he said.

"I did look at buying the club about 20 years ago, and it wasn't the right time for me, but I’d like to hope… they might not recognise it, but some of the advice I gave them did get their land back off the previous owner who'd tried to sell it for a pound.

"We have a long history, predominantly as rivals, but obviously, they play in the English system, we play in the Welsh, and historically, we have used it in Europe on a number of occasions back in the day."

The most memorable of those times came in 2005, less than a decade after Harris had taken over Welsh minnows Llansantfraid FC.

TNS - then named for his ex-company, Total Network Solutions - were drawn in a two-legged Champions League qualifier against holders Liverpool, mere months after the 'Miracle of Istanbul'.

11 TNS were unable to play Liverpool at their former ground Credit: Getty

11 The 2005 meeting between the two teams was the fastest ever sold-out Champions League first-round qualifier Credit: Getty

The team then played at a 2,000-capacity recreation ground that failed to meet UEFA requirements, leading to the Racecourse switch.

Harris added: "It was a great experience. I remember both legs extremely well. It's one where I think we put up a better fight than they were expecting.

"[Rafael Benitez], who was manager at the time, cancelled their summer training camp because he expected to win 7-8, 9-0, and we held them to a 3-0 defeat.

"But it took Steven Gerrard, an exceptional performance by him, to make the difference.

"I think if he'd have gone to Chelsea that summer, we could have been looking at a game that was a lot closer."

Ironically, that sentiment may have also applied had TNS managed to get Liverpool's all-time leading goalscorer to play against them!

11 Gerrard came off the bench to score twice at Wrexham's Racecourse Ground Credit: Getty

Liverpool icon almost came out of retirement at age 43 to face the Reds

Ian Rush, a two-time European Cup winner at Anfield, admitted he was nearly tempted into donning the boots at age 43.

“It got close,” he told the Echo in 2022. “Mike Harris, who is still the owner of TNS now, asked me if I would come out of retirement.

“It was nice to be asked, a good thing, and I did consider it. But I felt it wasn’t worth it.”

Harris explained to talkSPORT: "Ian Rush was a president of the club. He's a great friend of mine. There's a legendary interview on Sky if you can actually find it, but he came down to watch me play Sunday football, and the cameras were there.

"I scored, and they captured that moment on TV, and they were interviewing him later in the day and said, 'Hey Rushy, is it right you might be bringing your boots out?' And then somebody interrupted Rushy and said, ‘I don't think Rushy needs to get his boots out. The chairman can score as well’."

11 A plaque showing TNS's 'twinning' with Chelsea FC, and one to commemorate the opening of the stand by Ian Rush at The Recreation Ground Credit: Getty

Rush, who opened TNS' 500-seater stand four years prior, was involved when the club faced Manchester City in the 2003 UEFA Cup.

The Welsh side ultimately weren't 'dancing in the streets of Total Network Solutions' as famously suggested by talkSPORT's Jeff Stelling after suffering a 7-0 aggregate defeat.

But TNS still holds the honour of playing the first official match at the Etihad, something Harris admitted remains 'very special.'

"We've done quite a number of things, really," he claimed. "If you look at the qualifying rounds, the Liverpool game was the fastest ever sold-out Champions League game.

11 Man City beat TNS 5-0 in the first official game at what would become the Etihad Stadium Credit: Getty

"The game at Anfield, their first game, was sold out in about 30 minutes. It was also a sellout at Wrexham. When you add the two, it's the highest aggregate qualifying first-round ever.

"It was the same with the UEFA Cup, which we played City in; we had the full capacity there, which was at the time, 36,000 - we were the first competitive game they played at the City of Manchester Stadium, which is now the Etihad.

"Then, obviously groundbreaking that we played the reverse game at the Millennium Stadium. They're great days."

Liverpool icon Rush had helped coach TNS' strikers ahead of what was the Welsh outfit's first European match in 24 years against Man City.

11 Nicolas Anelka added the fifth for City Credit: Getty

And it nearly paid dividends for the club's current sporting director and Oldham Athletic assistant, Gary Brabin, in the second leg.

Unfortunately, ex-England goalkeeper David Seaman, famously lobbed by Ronaldinho at the World Cup 12 months earlier, had been rested for Nicky Weaver at the Millennium Stadium.

On the 5-0 first-leg loss at the Etihad, Harris said: "We played so well. We had a young goalkeeper in goal for us then, Gerard Doherty, who went on to play for us for many years.

"Great goalkeeper, only a young lad, perhaps 20 years old at the time.

11 Doherty bounced back from the City showing to earn plaudits from Rafa Benitez after the Liverpool tie Credit: Getty

"We would say that probably two or three of the goals were through his nervousness. But he went on to play some big games.

"The one disappointment I have is that Gary Brabin, in the return game at the Millennium Stadium, had a wicked shot from the halfway line, which, if they’d kept Seaman in goal, I think that would have been in the back of a net.

"The lad who they played instead that day, he was on the edge of his box, and Brabin put his head down and whacked it.

"It was going straight for the top corner, luckily enough, he just managed to run back at full pelt and tipped it over the bar."

11 After spotting Seaman off his line slightly, Ronaldinho created magic to leave the England star grasping at thin air Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Lukaku 'knocked out' Wales international

The Etihad is not the only stadium belonging to an English giant to share a history with TNS; a plaque honouring their brief partnership with Chelsea remains outside Stamford Bridge's Shed End.

And two former Blues stars make up the podium of best players Harris has seen against his side over the years.

Gianfranco Zola bagged a hat-trick in a 6-1 friendly win at Treflan Recreation Ground in Powys in 2002, eight years before 17-year-old Anderlecht substitute Romelu Lukaku bagged twice in a 3-0 triumph.

11 Lukaku held off Evans to score the first of his two goals against The New Saints Credit: AFP

11 The then-teenager scored twice after only fifteen minutes on the pitch Credit: AFP

Steven Gerrard, I think, is probably number one," Harris stated. "Then you've got to look at Lukaku, as the other, he was playing for Anderlecht then, before his move to Chelsea.

"Steve Evans, whose obviously had six caps for Wales, [Lukaku’s] got the ball knocked him over as if he wasn’t there, the next time he’s booted the ball and knocked him out.

"The guy’s a fantastic footballer. Obviously, that was in competitive games, and you’ve also gotta say, Gianfranco Zola, for his silky skills.

"He came and played piano in the clubhouse afterwards, and you know what, if he wasn’t a footballer, he could have been a pianist.

"He was [that good], and what a gentleman. You’ve gotta say he’s one of the most humble gentlemen I’ve ever met!"

Mike Harris stars in The Road to Europe - The Mike Harris Story, a football documentary like no other, which is available to buy or rent now on Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV.

Sports.title: Furious Jason Cundy clashes with pundit and tells Chelsea star to ‘keep your mouth shut’
Sports.content:
Furious Jason Cundy clashes with pundit and tells Chelsea star to ‘keep your mouth shut’

Jason Cundy was involved in a heated studio debate as he slammed Marc Cucurella for publicly criticising Chelsea's board.

In a recent bombshell interview, the Spaniard hit out at the Blues' youth-centric transfer policy and ownership decisions.

5 Marc Cucurella has caused a stir with his comments over the international break Credit: Getty

Prior to the international break, Liam Rosenior's side were on a nightmare run of form, having lost each of their last four matches.

This included a humiliating Champions League round of 16 exit, which saw them thrashed 8-2 on aggregate by Paris Saint-Germain.

Worse still, Chelsea find themselves at risk of missing out on qualification for Europe's premier competition next term, having dropped to sixth in the Premier League table.

What did Marc Cucurella say?

Still reeling from recent events, Cucurella voiced his concerns over the situation at Chelsea in brutal fashion.

The 27-year-old criticised the club's transfer policy under the BlueCo consortium, which has seen them focus on signing young players, claiming the Blues are lacking proven, high-quality options.

Speaking to the Athletic, he said of the PSG loss: “You are fighting and training every day only to realise, at the very end, that when games matter, we are still a bit away from the top level.

“I understand this is part of the club’s policy, and that they want to take this direction — signing young players and looking to the future.

"But, for all of us who are still here and want to win big things, moments like this make you feel discouraged."

In the same interview, Cucurella also questioned the board's decision to allow former boss Enzo Maresca to leave the club in January.

Cundy: Cucurella is part of problem

Cucurella's explosive comments caused a stir in the talkSPORT studios, with former Chelsea defender Jason Cundy left furious.

5 Cucurella said Enzo Maresca's mid-season departure had a big impact on Chelsea's players Credit: Getty

5 The Blues suffered a demoralising 3-0 defeat to Everton in their last match before the international break Credit: Getty

Appearing on talkSPORT's Inside Chelsea podcast, Cundy slammed the left-back for the timing of his comments and insisted his performances have contributed to the Blues' poor form

He began: “I understand his frustration because we all feel it as well.

“I find it interesting that he's chosen the words that he has - about fighting in training every day to realise [you don’t have the players].

“Right now, you are part of the problem, Cucurella. We are where we are and the performances, your levels have dropped."

Not everyone agreed with Cundy, however, as fellow pundit Matisse Armani argued Cucurella was right to be frustrated.

The Blues superfan insisted the Spain star could look to leave if the club's owners don't sign players capable of winning silverware.

5 Chelsea's nine permanent arrivals last summer were all aged 23 or under, including Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Pedro Credit: Getty

He said: "Cucurella is in his prime. He wants to win trophies. He's got two options.

"Either Chelsea are going to start moving in a way that prioritises winning trophies and winning at the highest level - which we can clearly see with the strategy and the model that is not the priority - or he's going to have to leave the football club because he wants to achieve things.

Admitting Cucurella has been underperforming recently, Armani claimed Chelsea's transfer policy places too much pressure on key players.

He added: “The likes of Cucurella, [Moises] Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez, and Reece James, their levels have dropped.

“But do you think they can carry this football club to where they want to get to?

"Or do you think they're going to need some help? Other players like Alejandro Garnacho, like Pedro Neto, who are nowhere near pulling their weight.”

5 Cucurella has played 41 games this season for club and country, but Cundy had little sympathy for his recent comments Credit: Getty

'Who the hell does he think he is?'

While Armani sympathised with Cucurella, Cundy only became more riled by his comments and tore into the defender.

Responding to Armani, he said: “I don’t disagree with you, but Cucurella’s paid a huge amount of money, right? Do your talking on the pitch.”

Continuing to slate the timing of his interview, the Sports Bar host added: “It would land better if he was putting in performances that were of a standard.

“His performances have dropped. Caicedo’s have dropped, Enzo’s. Everyone's performances have dropped.

“We are in a position now where the football club is in a real crucial period. And these comments are coming out from someone who I am seeing not putting in the levels.”

Rounding off his furious rant, Cundy raged: “Who the hell does he think he is? He's a player. You are paid to play football.

“Keep your mouth shut, do your job.”

Sports.title: Chelsea got it horribly wrong with Liam Rosenior and we all know who his successor will be
Sports.content:
Chelsea got it horribly wrong with Liam Rosenior and we all know who his successor will be

Chelsea broadcaster Matisse Armani believes the club's contradictory managerial strategy could force their best players to leave.

The Blues are on their second manager this season, having replaced Enzo Maresca with Liam Rosenior in January.

3 Palmer has struggled for form and fitness since Rosenior joined Chelsea Credit: Getty

It was an eyebrow-raising appointment given Rosenior came from Ligue 1 outfit Strasbourg, who are run by Chelsea's owners BlueCo.

Although Rosenior established himself as a name to watch among young English coaches, some questioned whether he was ready for the step up given he had only managed Hull City and Strasbourg without guiding them to silverware.

Not looking Rose-y

Rosenior's appointment also made him the fifth different permanent manager in the BlueCo era at Chelsea, with his predecessors including Thomas Tuchel, Graham Potter, Mauricio Pochettino and Maresca.

Despite a bright start to life with the Blues where he oversaw eight wins in his first 11 games, Rosenior's goodwill has largely dried up following a run of four consecutive defeats across all competitions.

The latest, a 3-0 loss away to Everton, left Chelsea six points adrift of fourth-placed Aston Villa in the race for Champions League football next season.

If results weren't enough of a concern, Rosenior now has to contend with questions over the futures of Enzo Fernandez, Cole Palmer and Marc Cucurella.

Summer of uncertainty?

Fernandez hasn't exactly been shy about his uncertain future, stating he doesn't know where he will be after the World Cup.

The Argentinian sent the rumour mill into overdrive when he claimed he could see himself living in Madrid.

Palmer is yet to publicly comment on his future, although reports recently emerged he was growing disgruntled at Stamford Bridge and has three European giants interested in signing him.

Cucurella then became the latest Blues star to plunge his Chelsea career into doubt when he didn't exactly shut down talk of a romantic return to Barcelona.

3 Cucurella claimed he would 'consider' a return to Barcelona if they came calling Credit: Getty

The loss of three important players would be a bitter pill to swallow for Rosenior and Chelsea fans alike.

Yet Matisse would not blame the trio, or any of their other stars, if they sought an exit.

'Rosenior wasn't hired on merit'

"No one can sit here and tell me that 28-year-old Cucurella, 27-year-old Reece James and whoever else is a top player in this team, is looking at that hiring of Liam Rosenior from Strasbourg, where they basically negotiated with themselves, their own feeder club, for their own manager who basically can't reject them because he's employed by them, and you can tell me that is on merit and it's in the best interests of Chelsea to hire a manager of that standard, absolutely impossible," Matisse said on the latest episode of Inside Chelsea.

"So if you're a top player like Cucurella, and I do believe you're a top five left-back in the world, why on earth would you not be angling for a move away from Chelsea?"

Worryingly, Matisse believes the club's approach with hiring Rosenior means fans and players alike know exactly who is likely to take the reins if and when a change is required.

Next man up

"We all know the next manager coming in after Liam Rosenior if there are any murmurs of any issues, if there is a lack of Champions League qualification, it is not going to be a top manager," Matisse said.

3 Rosenior's Chelsea tenure has quickly turned sour Credit: Getty

"We're talking about Gary O'Neil at Strasbourg, are we not?

"If I were a top player, I'd be angling for a move. They don't support Chelsea, they have their own careers, they have to be selfish.

"The board has shown already they will be quite selfish in terms of how quickly they'll chop and change the players.

"The players will leave and therefore you see your teammates leave so ruthlessly, you have every right to move the same way."

Regardless of who is in charge at Chelsea, Matisse believes little will change unless the board meticulously sticks to a plan regarding personnel on the pitch and in the dugout.

"You can't ask 21, 22, 23-year-olds to be jumping up and down different managers and different systems and different ideologies and thinking that's going to pan out well for you," Matisse said.

"You have to pick a struggle. If you're constantly going to chop and change managers and you're going to have players that can ride through those situations, or you're going to have a young team and build long-term with a manager."
